brief: Following the Fed's 25-basis-point hike, the market keeps pricing additional tightening even as financial conditions remain relatively accommodative by historical standards; RJ notes rate-hike cycles historically bring 8% to 10% pullbacks but equities have moved higher over the following 6-12 months when growth stays resilient. Leadership has rotated from average stocks and small caps toward mega-cap technology, with the Mag 7 breaking out to new highs after consolidating through 2026. Oil price declines have relieved pressure on the 10-year Treasury yield, supporting equity valuations and easing inflation pressure, even as the 2-year yield has risen on rate-hike pricing, flattening the curve and pushing bank stocks back to support. Oil and gas refiners have gained over 100% since the Iran conflict began but now trade nearly three standard deviations above their 200-day average, raising consolidation odds. A U.S. dollar breakout above resistance threatens the weak-dollar tailwind behind emerging markets' year-to-date outperformance. RJ expects near-term chop from headline noise and midterm elections but stays constructive longer-term.
